questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to experience studying law in an English speaking country (either U.S. or Australia) and San Diego has it all: Great weather year round, beaches, good vibes and lots of activities to do! It was also a great opportunity to travel (around the U.S. and Mexico) and establish international connections.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy, since the staff at University of San Diego had reached out to me upon arrival and I therefore knew who to contact with my questions. The university's website also contained a lot of helpful information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a whole week of mandatory introduction before classes started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: A little too much unnecessary information was given in the introduction week, but it was ok.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very challenging. Start looking for housing as soon as possible! Check fb pages on housing and Airbnb. If you haven't found housing before your arrival in San Diego, you should walk around the beach areas and look at the houses - usually there are signs on the houses with the landlord's contact information. I would recommend you to call all the phone numbers you see!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in Mission Beach, and it was amazing. I could relax on the beach and surf everyday, and you can walk to Pacific Beach, where there is a lot of restaurants/bars/clubs. I would definitely recommend living in the beach areas to get the full San Diego experience!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
If you want to live in the beach areas (Mission Beach, Pacific Beach) just know it is very expensive - however definitely worth it! 
The university cannot help you find housing off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: All other students (1. year, 2. year, 3. year and LL.M students) get to choose courses before the exchange students.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received an e-mail from the university regarding registration for classes, and attached was a list with courses to choose from. However, I was not informed that registration for courses was based on a first-come-first-serve principle. Therefore, I did not (initially) get the course I wanted, and I was told to sign up for the waitlist on the courses that I did not get. I didn't know how to do that, and they did not guide me through it, but in the end they did it for me, and I managed to get the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They responded through my e-mails. I kinda feel like they expected you to know their "system" and they were not very helpful when they just told me to "sign up for the waitlist".

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I got the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Reply as soon as you receive the e-mail about course registration. You should also know that in the first 2 weeks of classes, it is possible to change the courses you chose - so you have a chance to check out the courses you chose, and then later decide if you want to change it!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses was easier than the courses at UCPH. There was not a lot of preparation for classes.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In some classes they use the socratic method, but not in all of them. In some classes they don't use visuals (e.g., PowerPoint), so you just listen to the professor speaking in every class. The professors are all very engaged and they go a long way to make class interesting!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to U.S. Law
Law at the Movies
International Negotiation
Negotiation
Interviewing & Counseling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend taking Negotiation with Gregg Relyea. His classes are super informative, fun and I have learned a lot from him!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of social activities for law students, international students and a lot of (sports)clubs to join!

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would recommend going to the activities with the other exchange students so you can meet the (international) people at University of San Diego that does not go to the law school!
I would also recommend going to "Bar Review", which is a Friday bar for the law students! Posters will be up in the law school hallway with information about date, location etc.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Travel as much as you can! Visit Los Angeles (Cali), San Francisco (Cali), Route 1 (Cali), Yosemite National Park (Cali), Arizona, Utah, Las Vegas! 
You should also check out the different neighbourhoods of San Diego. La Jolla and Coronado (island) are really nice areas in San Diego.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to start the conversation. Americans are usually very open.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Find a house/apartment in one of the beach areas.
2. Don't use too much time studying - you will pass your exams. Instead, go travelling! 
3. Buy a surfboard and learn how to surf!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Remember to pack some warm clothes - it can be chilly in December/January/February.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to travel around the U.S., experiencing being a student at an American university, and meeting new people!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding housing.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: A semester at University of San Diego is the best experience I've had in my life! Enjoy it to the fullest.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
